learn: Key parent functions: linear, quadratic, cubic, square root, reciprocal, exponential, logarithmic, absolute value.
Each has a recognisable shape, domain and range.
Knowing parents makes graphing transformations quick.
check: y = 1/x has a vertical asymptote at...
lessons.try: Sketch eight parent functions from memory.

learn: Even: f(-x) = f(x), symmetric about the y-axis. Odd: f(-x) = -f(x), symmetric about the origin.
Piecewise functions use different rules on different intervals.
Step functions (like floor) jump between values.
lessons.try: Graph a piecewise function for a phone plan's cost.

learn: Add, subtract, multiply, divide and compose functions.
Inverses reflect over y = x.
Restrict domains to make functions invertible.
check: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 1, f(g(2)) is...
lessons.try: Find and graph the inverse of f(x) = (x - 1)³.

learn: End behaviour depends on degree and leading coefficient.
Zeros and multiplicity shape the graph.
The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a zero between sign changes.
check: A sign change between x = 1 and 2 guarantees a...
lessons.try: Sketch y = (x + 2)(x - 1)² from its zeros.

learn: Vertical asymptotes, holes, horizontal or slant asymptotes.
If the numerator's degree is one more, there is a slant asymptote.
Analyse sign charts to sketch graphs.
check: Degree of numerator less than denominator gives horizontal asymptote...
lessons.try: Fully analyse f(x) = (x² - 1)/(x - 2).

learn: Find critical points, then test intervals.
Exclude values that make denominators zero.
Write answers in interval notation.
y = ab^x and y = ae^(kx) model growth and decay.
k > 0 is growth; k < 0 is decay.
Logistic models level off at a carrying capacity.
check: Logistic models level off at a...
lessons.try: Model a virus spreading with a logistic curve.

learn: Product, quotient and power rules.
ln and e^x are inverses.
Change of base converts to any base.
lessons.try: Simplify ln(e³) + log(100).

learn: Isolate the exponential and take logs.
Combine logs and rewrite in exponential form.
Check for extraneous solutions with logs (arguments must be positive).
lessons.try: Solve log₂(x) + log₂(x - 2) = 3.

units.t: Trigonometric Functions and the Unit Circle

learn: π radians = 180°; arc length s = rθ.
Coterminal angles differ by 360° (2π).
Reference angles are the acute angle to the x-axis.
check: Arc length with r = 5, θ = 2 is...
lessons.try: Convert 10 angles between degrees and radians.

learn: sin θ = y, cos θ = x, tan θ = y/x.
Signs by quadrant: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine (ASTC).
Memorise values for 30°, 45°, 60°.
lessons.try: Fill a blank unit circle with exact values.

learn: y = A sin(B(x - C)) + D: amplitude A, period 2π/B, phase shift C, vertical shift D.
Tangent has period π and asymptotes.
Inverse trig functions have restricted ranges: arcsin gives -π/2 to π/2.
lessons.try: Graph y = 2 sin(x - π/4) + 1.

learn: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
Reciprocal and quotient identities.
lessons.try: Prove tanθ cosθ = sinθ.

learn: sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB.
cos 2θ = cos²θ - sin²θ; sin 2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ.
Use these to find exact values like sin 75°.
lessons.try: Find the exact value of cos 15°.

learn: Isolate the trig function, then find all solutions in a period.
Add multiples of the period for general solutions.
Factor when equations are quadratic in a trig function.
check: General solutions add multiples of the...
lessons.try: Solve 2 sin x - 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.

units.t: Sequences, Series and an Introduction to Limits

learn: Arithmetic and geometric series formulas.
Infinite geometric series converge when the ratio is between -1 and 1.
Repeating decimals are infinite geometric series: 0.333... = 1/3.
lessons.try: Write 0.272727... as a fraction.

learn: A limit is the value a function approaches as x approaches a point.
Limits can exist even where the function is undefined (a hole).
Notation: lim x→a f(x) = L.
check: A limit can exist at a...
lessons.try: Estimate a limit from a table of values.

learn: Average rate of change = (f(b) - f(a))/(b - a).
The instantaneous rate is the limit of average rates: the derivative idea.
Calculus builds on this in college or AP courses.
check: f(x) = x² from 1 to 3 has average rate...
The instantaneous rate is the idea behind the...
lessons.try: Estimate the speed of a falling object at t = 2 s from position data.

learn: Categorical data: bar charts and pie charts. Quantitative data: histograms, box plots, dot plots.
Describe shape, centre, spread and outliers (SOCS).
Avoid misleading graphs with truncated axes.
check: SOCS stands for shape, outliers, centre and...
lessons.try: Find a misleading graph in the media and fix it.

learn: Mean is sensitive to outliers; median is resistant.
Standard deviation measures typical distance from the mean; IQR = Q3 - Q1.
Outliers: beyond 1.5 × IQR from the quartiles.
lessons.try: Compute the five-number summary for a data set.

learn: Compare centres, spreads, shapes and outliers in context.
Use parallel box plots or back-to-back stem plots.
Write comparisons in complete sentences.
check: A skewed-right distribution has a long...
lessons.try: Compare test scores from two classes.

learn: P(A) is between 0 and 1; P(not A) = 1 - P(A).
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).
Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B).
check: P(at least one six in two rolls) is...
Two fair coin flips both heads is...
lessons.try: Find the probability of rolling at least one six in two rolls.

learn: P(A given B) = P(A and B)/P(B).
Two-way tables organise conditional probabilities.
Tree diagrams show sequences of events.
check: If P(A and B) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5, P(A given B) is...
Drawing 2 aces without replacement from 52 cards is...
lessons.try: Build a two-way table from survey data.

learn: Permutations (order matters): nPr = n!/(n - r)!. Combinations: nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!).
Expected value = Σ x·P(x).
Games of chance usually have negative expected value for players.
check: Casino games usually have ___ expected value for players.
lessons.try: Calculate the expected value of a raffle ticket.

learn: Normal curves are symmetric and bell-shaped, defined by mean and SD.
The 68-95-99.7 rule estimates proportions.
z-tables or technology give exact proportions.
check: A z-score of 0 is at the...
lessons.try: Find the proportion of heights above a given value.

learn: Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling.
Convenience and voluntary response samples are biased.
Randomisation reduces bias.
check: An online poll anyone can answer is ___ response.
lessons.try: Design a survey of your school with stratified sampling.

learn: Sample statistics vary from sample to sample.
The Central Limit Theorem: sample means are approximately normal for large samples.
Larger samples give less variability.
check: The CLT says sample means are approximately...
lessons.try: Simulate sample means with dice and plot them.

learn: A confidence interval is estimate ± margin of error.
95% confidence means the method captures the true value 95% of the time.
Larger samples shrink the margin of error.
check: A poll of 52% ± 3% gives the interval...
lessons.try: Interpret a poll's margin of error.

learn: Null hypothesis: no effect. Alternative: an effect.
A small p-value (often below 0.05) is evidence against the null.
Statistical significance is not the same as practical importance.
check: A p-value of 0.01 is ___ evidence against the null.
Significance is not the same as...
lessons.try: Design an experiment and state hypotheses.

learn: Correlation r ranges from -1 to 1 and measures linear strength.
The least-squares regression line predicts y from x.
Correlation does not prove causation; beware extrapolation.
check: Predicting far outside the data is...
lessons.try: Fit a regression line to real data and interpret the slope.
